sasha (eng-ml): quick heads-up — onboarding run for redwood-ggml-v2-int4 shows a reproducible divergence tied to KV prefill + very long context (>>16k). opening thread with minimal repro and logs.

olivia (eng-runtime): paste the minimal repro? is this on dedicated or hosted?

sasha (eng-ml): dedicated nightly (runtime 2.3.1, kernel fwd-v3). repro script (python) below — simple long prompt + repeated prefill. using prefill_stride=2048 and use_kv_prefill=True.

sasha (eng-ml): ```python
# minimal repro (local)
from redwood import Client
cli = Client(model='redwood-ggml-v2-int4', endpoint='https://internal-dedicated')
prompt = "System: keep state stable.\n" + ("A" * 32000)  # large body to trigger wrap/tiling
resp = cli.generate(prompt, max_tokens=512, use_kv_prefill=True, prefill_stride=2048)
print(resp.text[:400])
```

sasha (eng-ml): observed: fp16 baseline matches expected tokens across the full run. int4 path diverges consistently at ~18k tokens after a prefill boundary. toggling prefill_stride to 1024 moves the divergence point but does not remove it.

mike (eng-oncall): any stack traces or kv-index dumps? could be an off-by-one when we tile the KV shards during prefill.

sasha (eng-ml): attached log excerpt (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-19T22:04:12Z] prefill: stride=2048, prefill_chunks=16
[2026-03-19T22:04:12Z] kv_write idx_start=16384 idx_end=18431 shard=2
[2026-03-19T22:04:12Z] kv_read idx_start=16384 idx_end=18431 shard=2
[2026-03-19T22:04:30Z] generate: token=17995 token_text=\"the\"
[2026-03-19T22:04:30Z] generate: token=17996 token_text=\"cat\"
[2026-03-19T22:04:30Z] generate: token=17997 token_text=\"sat\"
[2026-03-19T22:04:30Z] generate: token=17998 token_text=\"on\"
[2026-03-19T22:04:30Z] generate: token=17999 token_text=\"the\"
[2026-03-19T22:04:30Z] generate: token=18000 token_text=\"mat\"
[2026-03-19T22:04:30Z] WARNING: kv-index-wrap between write/read detected: write_end=18431 read_end=18432
```

sasha (eng-ml): that WARNING is suspicious — read_end=18432 even though write_end=18431. looks like a single-token slip when converting between global pos -> shard tile pos.

kate (eng-ml): interesting — I recently saw a rotary scaling drift when converting rotary phase embeddings in int4 path. did you try forcing fp16 rotary math while keeping int4 KV storage?

sasha (eng-ml): yes — forcing fp16 rotary (ropegap_fix=true) mitigates severity but still ends up diverging after longer runs. suggests a combined effect: quantized KV store + small rotary precision change + tiling wrap.

olivia (eng-runtime): can you run with `KV_DEBUG_DUMP=true` for one run and drop the shard dumps into /tmp/sasha-kvdump.tar? also include kernel flag `--no-tiling` if possible to see if tiling is the trigger.

sasha (eng-ml): starting that now. I'll post the dump link when ready. expect ~1.2GB for full dump.

mike (eng-oncall): routing note — if this is an off-by-one in the tiling math we should triage as high. it can cause silent correctness regressions for long-context customers. adding oncall to loop. :rotating_light:

ci-bot: Build 2026-03-20T03:12:45Z: nightly-inference-tests failed on test-longctx-kv-integrity (job id: 8751). logs uploaded to: https://ci.internal/builds/8751/logs.txt

olivia (eng-runtime): thanks — I'll pull the CI logs and the KV dump once available. first quick check: is the global position calculation using int32 or int64 in the int4 path? if we accidentally truncated somewhere it could increment incorrectly at boundaries.

sasha (eng-ml): dump uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/sasha-kvdump/3312345678.tar.gz

kate (eng-ml): next steps I suggest:
- olivia, verify pos calculation and tiling floor/ceil logic
- mike, add a unit test that fuzzes prefill_stride boundaries and asserts kv read/write symmetry
- sasha, run same script on fp16 and int8 to confirm quantization curve

sasha (eng-ml): opened issue ML-2319 and linked CI failure + dump. assigning to @olivia. adding reproduction steps and minimal script. :+1:

olivia (eng-runtime): ack — will triage tomorrow morning (PST). preliminary suspicion: tiling boundary rounding + quantized pack/unpack alignment. will report back with a small reproducer patch.

mike (eng-oncall): leaving watch on ML-2319. if we see this in production telemetry we should trigger fallback to fp16 for affected customers.

sasha (eng-ml): thanks all. I'll run an overnight sweep with `--no-tiling` and `ropegap_fix=true` variants and leave results in the issue.

ci-bot: NOTE: incident template reminder — if this affects >3 customers, escalate to secops.

olivia (eng-runtime): quick follow after looking at dumps: there's indeed a `pos_map` entry where tile_end increments by +1 after quant pack. working on minimal patch.

kate (eng-ml): great, keep notes in ML-2319. prefer small revert-safe fix (adjust packing alignment) rather than big RPC change.

sasha (eng-ml): recorded a short Loom with the run and divergence visualization: https://loom.internal/sasha/kv-diverge-3312345678. will add to the issue.

mike (eng-oncall): thanks — good triage. keep us posted. :mag_right:
